title: GDP per head of 28 economies, 1929-1938 (Maddison Project Database 2023)
source: Maddison Project Database, version 2023 (J. Bolt and J. L. van Zanden), workbook 'mpd2023_web.xlsx', sheet 'Full data', DataverseNL, doi:10.34894/INZBF2
series: country (ISO code), year, gdppc_2011usd ('gdppc': real GDP per head in 2011 international dollars)
license: CC BY 4.0 (DataverseNL). The workbook's 'Notes' sheet sets a citation policy: 'CONDITIONS UNDER WHICH ALL ORIGINAL PAPERS MUST BE CITED: a) If the data is shown in any graphical form b) If subsets of the full dataset that include less than a dozen (12) countries are used for statistical analysis or any other purposes'. The chapter shows the data in a figure and cites the original sources listed in 'sources_by_country' (copied from the sheets 'Sources' and 'Maddison original sources', the rows whose period covers any of 1929-1938).
notes: Workbook SHA-256 ecc5916ca12789b983fc4be437f8a354bbf4291323605324ac3e0aea4c57cbb6 (the copy of Chapter 21). Poland has no figure for 1928, so the table begins in 1929; Czechoslovakia, Estonia and Latvia (in Bernanke and James's table of exits) have none for these years. China is left out: the database's listed source for China ends in 1933.
citation: Bolt, J. and J. L. van Zanden (2024), 'Maddison style estimates of the evolution of the world economy: A new 2023 update', Journal of Economic Surveys, doi:10.1111/joes.12618
